findings.location: Q4 §4, line beginning 'This is genuinely an orbifold setting. But it is a **different technical species**: continuous'; mirrored in VERDICT.md answer 5 at 'from interior eigenfunction data with a **triple-logarithmic** modulus — a different technical'
findings.issue: The one genuine counter-source — a paper whose title is literally 'quantitative stability of reconstruction for orbifolds' — is still dismissed with a label rather than an argument, while the decisive argument sits unused in the theorem Q4 itself quotes three lines earlier. Lassas–Lu–Yamaguchi's bound is stated on X ∖ S_{σ,δ}: a neighbourhood of the singular set is explicitly excised from the region the estimate covers, so LLY provides no quantitative control of cone data at all. That is a distinction a referee cannot argue with; 'different technical species' is a genre label that invites the reply 'so is every adjacent result'. Two further concrete grounds also go unstated: the input is interior eigenfunction restrictions on an open set, not the Laplace eigenvalue sequence; and the orbifolds are confined to the collapsing class MM(n,Λ,Λ_3,D), with bounds on curvature and its third covariant derivative, which the manuscript's triangle pillows need not satisfy. Note the asymmetry this creates within the deliverable: Q4 was revised to scope its Lipschitz/Hölder claim honestly, but the single named counterexample to its setting-novelty claim is still handled by assertion.
findings.evidence: Q4-stability.md quotes the theorem itself at the line '$$d_{GH}(X\setminus S_{\sigma,\delta},\hat X)<\frac{C_1(X,\sigma)}{(\log\log|\log\delta|)^{C_2}},$$' — the excision is already on the page. research/temp/claims-inverse-spectral-problems-for-collapsing-manifolds-ii-quantitative-stability-of.json, scope_conditions: 'Riemannian orbifolds arising as 1-dimensional Gromov-Hausdorff collapses of n-manifolds with bounded diameter, sectional curvature, and third covariant derivative of curvature (class MM(n,Lambda,Lambda3,D))' and 'interior spectral data of the weighted Laplacian on an open subset of a general n-1 dimensional orbifold limit space'. arXiv:2404.16448.
findings.suggested_fix: ANCHOR (Q4-stability.md, single line): 'This is genuinely an orbifold setting. But it is a **different technical species**: continuous' — REPLACE the 'different technical species' label and the sentence it heads with the three concrete grounds, keeping it to two or three sentences: (i) the estimate is stated on X ∖ S_{σ,δ}, i.e. a neighbourhood of the singular set is excised, so LLY gives no quantitative control of cone data whatsoever — the very invariant at issue here is outside its scope; (ii) the data are interior eigenfunction restrictions on an open set, not the eigenvalue sequence; (iii) the orbifolds are confined to the collapsing class MM(n,Λ,Λ_3,D). ALSO ANCHOR (VERDICT.md, single line): 'from interior eigenfunction data with a **triple-logarithmic** modulus — a different technical' — REPLACE the trailing label with ground (i) in compressed form, e.g. '…modulus — and one stated on the complement of a neighbourhood of the singular set, so it gives no quantitative control of cone data at all.'

findings.location: Q4 §5 item 4, line 'different statement from anything in the numerical-analysis literature, it is the natural'; mirrored in VERDICT.md answer 5 at 'blow-up appearing as the degradation of $\epsilon$. That statement has no counterpart in the'
findings.issue: Q4 correctly deflates the technique claim — Batenkov–Yomdin already own the conditioning half, and Q4 warns in terms that presenting it as new 'would be caught immediately by a referee with a numerical-analysis background' — and then commits the identical error one section later on the integer-valuedness. 'Once the error falls below half the minimum gap, recovery is exact' is the standard on-grid / integer-parameter exact-recovery argument, used throughout super-resolution, Prony with integer nodes, and compressed-sensing support recovery: the same literature Q4 has just finished citing. None of the eight documented queries touches 'integer', 'on-grid', 'exact support recovery' or 'quantization', so 'no counterpart in the numerical-analysis literature' is supported by nothing in this sweep. This is now the most exposed unqualified claim left in Q4, and it is exposed to precisely the referee Q4 tells the author to fear. The finding is not that the manuscript's theorem is unoriginal — it is that the deliverable asserts a negative it did not test, in the one place where it had already demonstrated the discipline of not doing so.

Q4-stability.md §4's eight-query list contains no integer/grid/quantization query. Contrast the revised 'Scope this claim honestly' passage in §3, which applies exactly the right discipline to the Lipschitz/Hölder claim and is the model this passage should follow.

findings.location: §1.2 Takeuchi, the bullet beginning '**Caveat on how much this could change:** commensurable Fuchsian groups have covolumes in'
findings.issue: Q1 was revised to handle the Takeuchi commensurability risk well — it now names Maclachlan–Reid, Voight and Singerman as untried routes to the class assignment. But outstanding-fetches.md §1.2 was not updated and still carries the original defence, which is logically inverted: it argues that 'commensurable Fuchsian groups have covolumes in rational ratio, not generally equal… so even a positive answer would not by itself make the manuscript's Theorem B prior art'. That rebuts an implication nobody needs. Nobody claims commensurability implies equal covolume; the risk is that Takeuchi's commensurability paper tabulates the 85 triples class by class with their covolumes and indices, so an equal-covolume pair sitting inside one class is displayed on the page — which is exactly what 'the coincidence appears in print' means. The effect is that the review's own register of open risks understates the item it simultaneously calls 'the single highest-value outstanding item in the review', and it now contradicts the more careful treatment in Q1. Two deliverables giving different accounts of the same risk is worse than either account alone.
findings.evidence: review/outstanding-fetches.md §1.2 states in the preceding bullet that 'Neither source assigns commensurability classes to individual triples' and in the following bullet that this is 'the single highest-value outstanding item in the review'. Q1-diophantine-novelty.md now reads 'Three routes were not exhausted and should be, before submission: Maclachlan & Reid's … Voight's *Quaternion Algebras*, and Singerman's work on triangle-group inclusions.' Both (2,8,8) and (3,3,12) are confirmed on Takeuchi's Theorem 3 list (J. Math. Soc. Japan 29 (1977) 91–106, DOI 10.2969/jmsj/02910091) and both have area π/4 by Gauss–Bonnet, so an equal-covolume pair is exactly what a class table would surface.
findings.suggested_fix: ANCHOR (single line): '**Caveat on how much this could change:** commensurable Fuchsian groups have covolumes in' — REPLACE the inverted defence with a correct statement of the exposure and a pointer to Q1: keep the true observation that commensurability does not imply equal covolume, but state that this is not where the risk lies — Takeuchi's class tables list covolumes and indices within each class, so an equal-covolume pair inside a single class would be visible in print and would have to be cited and distinguished. Add a clause noting that the class assignment may be obtainable without the 1977 paper via the secondary routes now listed in Q1-diophantine-novelty.md (Maclachlan–Reid, Voight, Singerman), so the item is 'fact not yet checked' rather than 'fact unobtainable'.

findings.location: '## The load-bearing caveat' and the two-part statement that follows it; cross-referenced from Q2-cone-coefficients.md at 'Full details, including the caveat structure, in `review/hyperresearch/APPENDIX-ncone-computation.md`.'
findings.issue: This is the reverse failure — a hedge that should now commit. The appendix's caveat conditions the whole n=4 result on 'Whether $b_2$ actually delivers $P_5$ with a nonzero coefficient at constant curvature is precisely question Q2, and it is not settled by this computation', then instructs that the result 'should be stated to the author in two parts', the second being 'Conditional on $b_2 \to P_5$'. Q2 has since settled that question affirmatively and cross-validated it: Schueth's Theorem 4.1 at constant curvature delivers P_5 with coefficient 1/2520, and the Uçar-derived p_2 was checked against it to symbolic zero. The conditional is discharged, but the appendix still presents it as live and Q2 still routes the author there 'including the caveat structure'. An author following that pointer will state a weaker two-part conditional result than the evidence now supports, and will read a live dependency where none remains. Worse, the caveat names the wrong dependency: the live conditionality for n≥4 is not the coefficient question at all but the isometry-versus-multiset issue Q2 now raises via the Thurston/Troyanov moduli-dimension argument, which the appendix does not mention.
findings.evidence: APPENDIX-ncone-computation.md '## The load-bearing caveat': '**Whether $b_2$ actually delivers $P_5$ with a nonzero coefficient at constant curvature is precisely question Q2**, and it is not settled by this computation'. Q2-cone-coefficients.md §3 settles it: Schueth Theorem 4.1 at constant curvature gives the 1/2520 coefficient on P_5, and the ℓ=2 row 'was cross-validated against **Schueth's Theorem 4.1**… the difference simplifies **identically to zero**'. Q2 §4 separately establishes the genuinely live caveat for n≥4 — that K(F) as defined is an isometry-class notion and the moduli space of n-cone spherical/constant-curvature metrics has real dimension 2n−6 (Thurston, DOI 10.2140/gtm.1998.1.511; Troyanov, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9947-1991-1005085-9).
